tasks.title: Bring the operator docs and the scope doc up to the merged check tiers
tasks.summary: Plan v5. Seven doc corrections from the closing spec review: the admitting `bs wave check` form, both index rows, the three 'only command that sees the branch' passages, queue-and-gate.md sections 4 and 5, and two sentences of the scope doc's red handling.
tasks.objective: Close seven closing-review findings whose stale text sits in docs that only merged tasks claimed, by rewording in place. Add no section, flag, code or test. (1) f-bs-check-tiers/integration-5e675a89: docs/guide/operator-guide/wave.md section 2 shows the admitting `bs wave check` form and names the post-merge refusals. (2) f-bs-check-tiers/integration-d01683bf: both index rows of the check-tiers scope doc say it shipped. (3) f-bs-check-tiers/integration-453b7376: closing-an-epic.md section 7a (its heading, first paragraph and contents-list line in docs/guide/operator-guide.md), limitations.md and status.md stop calling `bs integration check` the only run that sees the assembled branch. (4) f-bs-check-tiers/integration-af01945d: queue-and-gate.md section 4 shows `--checks` and says when the pre-merge tier replaces `--test-cmd`. (5) f-bs-check-tiers/integration-f82435f9: queue-and-gate.md section 5's overlay bullet names the layouts that have no overlay and the one known wrong case. (6) f-bs-check-tiers/integration-d1a46ec1 and (7) f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9c2b1d5e: docs/specs/check-tiers-scope.md names the revert-only `red-at-base` and the `no-pre-merge-checks` refusal. The epic spec's D4, D8 and AC6 already state what the merged code does; these docs follow them.
acceptance_criteria: 5e675a89. In docs/guide/operator-guide/wave.md section 2 (from `## 2.` to the `### \`bs wave next\`` heading), the first fenced example becomes the admitting form: `bs wave check factory/specs/active/epic-1/plan-v1.json epic-1/task-1 epic-1/task-2` with `--session <session-id> --plan-version <n> --causal-parent <event-id> --checks <checks.json> --project <project-dir>` (a `\` continuation is fine). The output block after it stays (it already shows only the `valid` key of what the verb prints). One new paragraph right after that block says three things, in this order. With `--checks`, which needs `--project` and `--session`, a task that waits on a merge no post-merge record certifies is refused `wave.held-by-post-merge`. With `--session` and no `--checks`, an epic whose log holds tiered integration records is refused `wave.checks-required`. A check without `--session` admits nothing and reads no log, so it checks neither refusal: it prints its verdict for a wave refused for claims, coupling or budget, and for an admissible wave it stops at `cli.missing-flag` before writing unless `--dry` is given, which writes nothing (a11671d4). Check: in section 2, `/usr/bin/grep -nE` finds `--session`, `--checks` and `--project` inside the first fenced block, and finds each of `wave.held-by-post-merge`, `wave.checks-required` and `--dry` at least once in the new paragraph.

d01683bf. The check-tiers-scope.md row of docs/specs/README.md's Scopes table and the specs/check-tiers-scope.md row of docs/README.md each say `(status: shipped)` where they now say `(status: planned)`. No other word of either row changes. Check: `/usr/bin/grep -nE 'check-tiers-scope.*status: planned' docs/specs/README.md docs/README.md` prints nothing, and `/usr/bin/grep -cE 'check-tiers-scope.*status: shipped'` prints 1 for each of the two files.

453b7376. Three passages stop saying `bs integration check` is the only run that sees the assembled integration branch. They are: closing-an-epic.md section 7a's heading and first paragraph; the limitations.md bullet beginning 'Nothing runs the integration-root check for you'; and status.md's item '**2. Some checks only run when you run them.**'. Each passage adds, in at most two sentences, the same fact. When the effective checks hold a post-merge entry, `/bs run` starts `bs checks post-merge` after each landing, and a batch that is due runs that tier at the integration head in a detached scratch worktree. `bs integration check` stays the clone-root run that close requires. In the first paragraph of section 7a, the sentence 'Every gate in this factory runs inside a task worktree.' is scoped to task gates, and so is the limitations.md bullet's second sentence ('Every automatic gate runs inside a task worktree (§7a).', wrapped across two source lines). The section 7a heading keeps its `## 7a.` prefix and `bs integration check`, and drops 'the only command that sees the branch'. Its line in docs/guide/operator-guide.md's contents list changes to the same text, linked by the new heading's GitHub anchor. The bold first sentence of the limitations.md bullet, which wraps 'the only' and 'check that sees' across two source lines, is reworded too. Check (newlines folded by `-z`, so a wrapped claim is caught; on the base it lists operator-guide.md, limitations.md, closing-an-epic.md and status.md): `/usr/bin/grep -rlzE 'only[[:space:]]+(command|check)[[:space:]]+that[[:space:]]+sees|only-command-that-sees' docs/guide` prints nothing (dcb34110); `/usr/bin/grep -nE 'checks post-merge'` prints at least one line in each of the three files; `/usr/bin/grep -cF 'Every gate in this factory runs inside a task worktree.' docs/guide/operator-guide/closing-an-epic.md` prints 0; and the contents-list link's anchor is the new heading's GitHub anchor (lower-cased, backticks and the em dash dropped, spaces to hyphens), written out in `notes`.

af01945d. In docs/guide/operator-guide/queue-and-gate.md section 4 (from `## 4.` to the next `## ` heading), the fenced `bs queue run` example gains `--checks checks.json`. The paragraph on the cumulative regression gate gains one sentence. With `--checks` and an entry whose effective tier is later than pre-merge (declared or from the overlay), the pre-merge tier is the pre-landing test and neither `--test-cmd` nor `--select-test-cmd` runs. The landing records `pre_landing: pre-merge-tier` and names its `queue-tier-run` record by `pre_landing_run_id`; the sentence points to section 5. Check: `/usr/bin/grep -nE` finds `--checks` inside section 4's fenced block, and finds `pre-merge-tier` and `queue-tier-run` in section 4.

f82435f9. In queue-and-gate.md section 5 (from `## 5.` to `## 5a.`), the overlay bullet ('**The tier overlay.**') replaces 'outside a repository' with the layouts that have no overlay, in one sentence. They are: outside a git repository; a bare repository; an absorbed submodule, whose git dir lives in the superproject's `.git/modules/` (a submodule whose `.git` is its own directory is an ordinary repository and keeps its overlay at its own root); and a `--separate-git-dir` layout. In each, writes are refused with `checks.overlay-not-a-repo` and proposals carry no items, so no tier is learned there. One more sentence names the known wrong class: every linked worktree of a `--separate-git-dir` layout whose git dir is named `.git` resolves the overlay to that git dir's parent, not to the work tree (deaf22c9). The bullet's other sentences stay. Check: `/usr/bin/grep -nE` in section 5 finds `submodule`, `.git/modules`, `bare`, `--separate-git-dir` and `checks.overlay-not-a-repo`.

d1a46ec1. In docs/specs/check-tiers-scope.md's list 'A red must have run, and must reproduce, before any bisect.', step 4 names its outcome: a red at a base not yet observed green is `red-at-base`, and there the failure predates the batch. Step 5 gains one sentence. When every task merge in the range is green and only a landed bs revert commit after them turns the head red, the outcome is also `red-at-base`: no task is blamed, nothing is promoted, and the result names the revert in `red_after_revert`. The sentence 'A red that predates the batch promotes nothing.' under 'Decline and promotion' stays word for word, because checkTiersScopeDoc.test.ts pins it. Check: `/usr/bin/grep -nE 'red_after_revert' docs/specs/check-tiers-scope.md` prints one line inside that list.

9c2b1d5e. The scope doc's '**A tested and recorded revert.**' bullet gains one sentence. When the effective checks hold no pre-merge entry, the revert cannot be tested, so none is built and no ref moves. The outcome is `revert-not-applicable` with reason `no-pre-merge-checks`; the culprit is still named, so automatic promotion still runs for its failing checks. Check: `/usr/bin/grep -nE 'no-pre-merge-checks' docs/specs/check-tiers-scope.md` prints a line inside that bullet.

Diff check (AC13), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff --no-renames <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout. An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

functional_clauses: The operator guide's `bs wave check` example is the form that admits, and its section 2 names `wave.held-by-post-merge`, `wave.checks-required` and the fact that nothing is admitted without `--session`.

No doc this task claims calls `bs integration check` the only run that sees the assembled branch; each of the three passages names the post-merge batch beside it, and section 7a's contents-list link still resolves.

Both index rows say the check-tiers scope shipped; queue-and-gate.md section 4 shows `--checks` and points to section 5; section 5 names the layouts with no overlay and the known wrong class; and the scope doc names the revert-only `red-at-base` and the `no-pre-merge-checks` refusal.
nonfunctional_clauses: Read factory/specs/active/bs-check-tiers/epic-spec.md before starting: D4, D8, AC6 and the section '### Plan v5 — closing-review fixes'. They state what the merged code does, and these docs follow them. Do not edit it: it sits outside every task's claims. Put one Progress line for this task in the result `notes` (what changed, and anything a later task must know); the epic session copies it in at merge.

Base: the epic's integration branch `bs/bs-check-tiers/integration` at 2c89aa5a or later, where every task of plan v4 has merged. If a passage a criterion names is not on the base as quoted, stop and report it in `notes` instead of rewriting another passage.
Diff budget (#511): `diff_lines` caps the non-test lines of the diff only. This task changes no test file, so every changed line counts.

No test is added or changed. Each criterion names the grep that checks it: run each one and put the command and its output in `notes`. The existing doc guards that read these files run in the full suite and must pass unchanged. Among them are docCommands.test.ts (every documented `bs` command and flag must exist in usage.ts), docErrorCodes.test.ts (every backticked dotted token must be a code raised in source), checkTiersScopeDoc.test.ts, checkTiersPlaybook.test.ts and handbackPreflight.test.ts.

Before hand-back run, in the foreground and in full: `pnpm run build`, root `pnpm run test` (the whole suite, never a scoped file), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test` and `pnpm exec biome check .` from the repo root (the whole repo, never a scoped path); report each exit code and the tail of each output. Run the full suite through `bs heavy run` so it takes the machine's heavy lock.
Also run `bash scripts/check.sh` and read the tail of its output, not only its exit code; name every step it printed as SKIP.

Weaken nothing: add no `.skip`, `.only`, `.todo`, `.fails`, `retry`, quarantine list or flaky marker; raise no `testTimeout`, `hookTimeout`, `timeout_ms`, `waitForLines` default, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` or any other timeout; remove, loosen or reorder no existing assertion, check, gate stage, grader, judge, review round or verifier.

Reword in place. Add no section, heading, flag or test. The only heading that changes is section 7a's, and the only claimed file outside the passages the findings name is docs/guide/operator-guide.md, for that heading's contents-list line. Cite no line numbers in the docs.

Open source, any stack: no other project's name, no client code and no absolute home-directory path (`/Users/...`, `/home/...`) in any committed file, and no sentence that names a per-stack tier default or makes anything require GitHub Actions.
Add no runtime or dev dependency.
Do not edit anything under factory/policies/.
Do not edit CHANGELOG.md: this task changes no behaviour, and the Unreleased Check tiers entry stands as written.
